summary: Forgotten Explorers is a 10-page space comic about old rovers left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through friendly characters and real space facts, it shows young readers that even after a rover's mission ends, its discoveries help scientists build better missions and guide the explorers of tomorrow.
details:
What it does: Our project is a 10-page space comic about rovers left behind on the Moon and Mars. In Part 1, an astronaut finds an old lunar rover that explains how it helped explore the Moon. In Part 2, a new Mars rover meets an older one that searched for signs of water. The comic shows that even after a rover’s mission ends, its discoveries keep helping future explorers. Each part ends with a real Space Fact.

Benefits: It makes space science fun and easy to understand for kids and beginners. It mixes storytelling with real facts, and it is short and easy to share in schools, libraries, and online.

Intended impact: We want readers to see that space exploration builds on the work of earlier missions. We hope to spark curiosity about the Moon and Mars and inspire readers to become future explorers.

Tools used: We wrote and planned the story in Google Docs, designed the illustrations and comic panels in Canva, and exported the final comic as a PDF. We worked on laptops and used NASA’s website for research on the Moon and Mars rovers.

Creativity: We gave the rovers personalities and voices so they tell their own stories. We used flashbacks, discovery panels, and a blueprint panel to explain science visually. The matching Moon and Mars stories show the same idea on two different worlds.

Factors considered: We aimed the comic at young readers by using simple language. We checked the scientific facts, kept the comic to 10 pages, and made the story emotional so readers care about the rovers. We chose PDF so it is easy to view and print.
